conditions: The declaration is an ordinary nonlocal statement in a nested function or class body.

An enclosing binding is eligible only if it is a function-local binding and is available to the declaration under lexical name resolution. An intervening function's global declaration for the name can make an otherwise enclosing binding unavailable.
limitations: Eligibility concerns a lexical binding, independently of whether the bound value has been initialized at runtime.
Module globals, class attributes, and type parameters in annotation scopes do not supply eligible function-local bindings.
Other declaration errors, including a prior use or assignment in the declaring block, are outside the binding-selection rule.
The compiler behavior and runtime examples used to challenge applicability are specific to the noted CPython revisions.

triggers: Controlling edition erratum, correction, or material counterexample.

statement: The Python 3.13.0 Language Reference documents that a nonlocal declaration in a nested function or class body selects the nearest eligible, lexically visible enclosing function-local binding for each declared name. A declared name with no eligible enclosing function-local binding causes SyntaxError at compile time.
